To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) neurons in primate dorsal anterior cingulated cortex encode a decision variable that signals the relative value of staying in a depleting food patch or leaving it to exploit a new patch; and, (2) this neural signal is modulated by the time it takes to get to the next patch, which is a critical component of the foraging task.
Neurons in the primate anterior cingulate encode a decision variable that signals the relative value of staying in a depleting patch or traveling to a new one.
